'''Bangala''' or {{lang|bxg|Mɔnɔkɔ na bangála}} is a [[Bantu languages|Bantu language]] spoken in the northeast corner of the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], it is also spoken in parts of [[South Sudan]] and some speakers are still found in the extreme western part of [[Uganda]] (e.g., [[Arua]], [[Koboko]]). A sister language of [[Lingala]], it is used as a [[lingua franca]] by people with different languages and rarely as a first language. In 1991 there were an estimated 3.5 million second-language speakers.<ref name=e25/> It is spoken to the east and northeast of the area where Lingala is spoken. In Lingala, Bangala translates to "People of [[Mongala]]". This means people living along the [[Mongala River]]. Across Bas-Uele Province, Bangala speakers have to a great extent adopted Lingala.

==History==
As Lingala spread east and north, its vocabulary was replaced more and more by local languages, and it became more of an [[interlanguage]] (a language that is a mix of two or more languages) and was classified as a separate language – Bangala. The vocabulary varies, depending on the first language of the speakers.

{{citation needed span|Around the 1980s, with the popularity and increased availability of Lingala in modern music,|date=December 2022}} young people in large villages and towns began adopting Lingala so much that their Bangala is becoming more of a dialect than a separate language.<ref name=e25/>

==Characteristics==
In Bangala, the words for six and seven ({{lang|bxg|motoba, sambo}}) are replaced with the [[Swahili language|Swahili]] words {{lang|sw|sita}} and {{lang|sw|saba}}. Many Lingala words are replaced by words in Swahili, [[Zande language|Zande]], other local languages, plus English ({{lang|bxg|bilizi}} is derived from the English word bridge) and French.

The verb "to be" is conjugated differently in Bangala. Below is a comparison with Lingala.

|-

|-
| he/she is || {{lang|ln|azali}} || {{lang|bxg|(yé) azí}}
|-
| it is || {{lang|ln|ezali}} || {{lang|bxg|(angó) azí}}
|-
| we are || {{lang|ln|tozali}} || {{lang|bxg|ɓísú azí}}, sometimes {{lang|bxg|tazí}}, less often {{lang|bxg|tozí}}
|-

The verb prefix {{lang|ln|ko-}}, meaning "to" in Lingala is instead {{lang|bxg|ku-}}, as it is in Swahili, so "to be" in Bangala is {{lang|bxg|kusara}}, not {{lang|ln|kosala}}. Many other Bangala words have an {{IPA|/u/}} sound where Lingala has an {{IPA|/o/}} sound, such as {{lang|bxg|ɓisu}} (not {{lang|ln|biso}} - "we") and {{lang|bxg|mutu}} (not {{lang|ln|moto}} - "person").

==Documentation==
Several old missionary sketches exist, most of them from the late 19th and early 20th century, e.g., Wtterwulghe (1899), MacKenzie (1910), Heart of Africa Mission (1916), van Mol (1927). However, Bangala as described in these concise overview sketches has changed over the past one hundred years, due to language contact with Ubangian languages and Nilo-Saharan languages of northeastern DR Congo. Currently, researchers from Ghent University, JGU Mainz and Goethe-Universität Frankfurt are working on a grammatical description of the language.
